task_instance: Build a security ownership map for a small sample git repo (people-to-file bipartite graph, bus factor, sensitive-code ownership, co-change clustering) and query it, following the skill's documented workflow: run scripts/run_ownership_map.py to produce ownership-map-out/ (people.csv, files.csv, edges.csv, cochange_edges.csv, summary.json, communities.json, cochange.graph.json, cochange.graphml), then run scripts/query_ownership.py to answer 'orphaned sensitive code', 'auth files with bus factor <= 1', and 'who touches sensitive code most'.
evidence: The skill package (openai__skills__security-ownership-map) ships only SKILL.md + LICENSE in this benchmark's ce_sources dir -- the referenced scripts/run_ownership_map.py and scripts/query_ownership.py are not present. Since the runtime fully supports everything the skill needs (git, python3, pip-installable networkx, filesystem writes), I reimplemented a faithful minimal version of both scripts from the SKILL.md spec to test the actual deliverable rather than being blocked by a missing file. Steps taken: (1) `pip install networkx` succeeded (networkx 3.6.1). (2) Created a small synthetic git repo at sample-repo/ with 3 authors (alice@corp, bob@corp, carol@corp), commits touching auth/, crypto/, a .pem file, app/, network/, and a lockfile, with controlled dates so some sensitive files are 'orphaned' (last touched before 2024). (3) Wrote run_ownership_map.py implementing: git log parsing (author/committer identity, date field, merge exclusion), default sensitivity rules (auth/crypto/*.pem), default co-change glue-file excludes (lockfiles/.github), Jaccard co-change graph, greedy-modularity community detection via networkx with per-community maintainers, and all documented output artifacts. (4) Wrote query_ownership.py implementing the people/files/person/file/summary sub-commands per the doc's examples. (5) Ran `python3 run_ownership_map.py --repo sample-repo --out ownership-map-out --emit-commits --graphml` -- produced people.csv, files.csv, edges.csv, cochange_edges.csv, commits.jsonl, communities.json, cochange.graph.json, cochange.graphml, summary.json in /tmp/.../ownership-map-out/. Verified summary.json correctly matches the doc's schema, e.g. orphaned_sensitive_code lists auth/login.py, auth/session.py, crypto/tls.rs, server.pem (all bus_factor=1, last touch before 2024); hidden_owners lists alice@corp '100% of auth code', bob@corp '100% of crypto code', alice@corp '100% of secrets code'; bus_factor_hotspots matches orphaned set here. Verified people.csv has commits/sensitive_touches/timezone columns; files.csv has bus_factor and tags columns; cochange_edges.csv has correct Jaccard weights (auth/login.py<->auth/session.py = 0.5); communities.json groups files with per-community maintainer rankings; cochange.graph.json is valid NetworkX node-link JSON with community_id/community_maintainers node attributes; cochange.graphml parses as valid GraphML. (6) Ran query_ownership.py 'summary --section orphaned_sensitive_code', 'files --tag auth --bus-factor-max 1', 'people --sort sensitive_touches', and 'person --person alice@corp' -- all returned correct bounded JSON slices matching the underlying CSVs/summary. This confirms the skill's core deliverable (git-history-derived ownership/bus-factor/sensitivity graph with CSV/JSON export and a query helper) is fully achievable in this runtime with only standard, freely installable tools (git, python3, networkx) -- no credentials, network services, or restricted capabilities were needed.
